## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix mixed-case writes so the new setter preserves the cache’s case-insensitive lookup contract.

## Changes

The pull request adds `Cache.set`, raises the default TTL from 60 to 300 seconds, and adds tests for round trips, the default TTL, and expiry.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Normalize keys in `Cache.set` — On a fresh cache, `set("ALPHA", 2)` followed by `get("ALPHA")` returns `None`. The setter stores `key` unchanged, while `get` looks up `key.lower()`. — A mixed-case update can also leave callers reading an older value stored under the lowercase key.

## Suggestions

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Expire entries at their deadline — With `ttl=1`, an entry written by `set` at monotonic time `1000.0` remains readable at `1001.0`. The setter records `1001.0` as the deadline, but `app/cache.py:21` treats equality as unexpired. — A lookup at the configured deadline can serve a value whose TTL has elapsed. — Fix: Use `expires <= time.monotonic()` in `app/cache.py:21`.
- app/cache.py:8 — tests — Verify the default TTL through cache lookups — The tests never look up an entry from `Cache()` after 61 seconds, when it should still be available. The default TTL test checks the class constant, and the expiry test supplies `ttl=1`. — A regression that restores 60-second expiry for default-constructed caches could pass the suite. — Fix: Extend `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` to check expiry through `Cache()` with a mocked clock.
